title: The archangels’ shrines, and the writer’s loyalty to his intercessors
english: …and at times a hard road at that, to see it through, as people who expect to find in you a greater goodwill toward their petition, and from God a share in the good things of those who strive eagerly for what is good. For in his holy churches, in the houses of prayer and the shrines of the martyrs, as in other heavens, he has set out his unfailing good things. And from the gifts that he himself, “the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule” (1 Timothy 6:15), has given and gives every day to each, from these he receives the bloodless sacrifice offered with piety and holiness, and he has every honour that men can give.

And I think that in the case against the heretics and in the things of theology even the brute beasts, nay rather the very stones, eagerly join their voices with ours. For what does love for God not do? Or to what does the heart’s true love give way?

For you know (but let all be said with God) that, with you and with the saints who came from our own nature interceding for me, I have so conducted myself that no one, even to this day, has yet chosen to bring against me any suit, so to speak, not even one for slander, on behalf of you, our intercessors, who receive from all people honours that match your measure. No one has summoned me by name to trial and judgment on this charge, though there are people to be found who accuse others of things that never happened. No one has even tried to convict me of having heard words spoken against God the Word and the Holy Spirit and then, perhaps from respect for the speaker or fear of him, of having nodded assent and praised what was not good; or of having ever been wholly negligent and treated with unbecoming slackness the duty of resisting as far as my strength allowed. On the contrary, many say that in such matters I always came forward vigorous and gentle, whether to answer for myself or to call others to account.

For I rightly count it the greatest gain, and an eternal one, for myself, for those who come from me and for those who are with us, to choose every toil, if need be, and every danger for the sake of him who made us and saves us, and who is able to judge, and to show loving-kindness on account of it: Father and Son and Holy Spirit.

Knowing, then, as chosen worshippers of the all-holy Trinity and intercessors for the human race, that after the Trinity itself, the cause of all and the giver of life, I have left nothing lacking in the reverence toward you that is owed to those who plead my cause with the Trinity, who supplies thoughts and wise words, both to itself…

added_allusions.reason: God receives the bloodless sacrifice “from the gifts he has given” (ἀφ᾽ ὧν ... δέδωκεν ... ἀπὸ τούτων ... δέχεται), the thought of David’s “of your own have we given you” and the liturgical offering formula. Not quoted; not cited inline.
“Even the very stones join their voices with ours” may echo “the stones would cry out”. Not quoted; not cited inline.

translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u19): retranslated from the Greek. The old English was garbled throughout (opening 'they have even relaxed their efforts', 'pleasant and martyric places', 'there is a readiness to agree with us', 'true charm yields to the heart', 'all-encompassing Trinity', the closing period turned into 'I owe these wise reminders to her') and lost the address to the archangels. Reference fixed: (Rev 19:16) -> 1 Timothy 6:15, whose Greek wording Didymus quotes.
